title: The Report Printer
briefing: It's the end of the week, and head office wants THE report: how many GPUs each line built, the fault rates, the worst day, and the best model. The data's in a CSV file. pandas turns it into a table you can slice, filter and group in a few lines. Nail this and the GPU floor is done!
hints: df = pd.read_csv("gpu_week.csv") loads the file. A column is df["built"], and you can make a new column with df["good"] = df["built"] - df["faulty"] (it works on every row at once, like NumPy).

Filter rows with df[df["built"] > 100]. df["fault_rate"].idxmax() gives the row label of the biggest value, then df.loc[label, "day"] reads the day. df.groupby("model")["good"].sum() totals per model.

df = pd.read_csv("gpu_week.csv") / df["good"] = df["built"] - df["faulty"] / df["fault_rate"] = df["faulty"] / df["built"] * 100 / busy = df[df["built"] > 100] / worst_day = df.loc[df["fault_rate"].idxmax(), "day"] / by_model = df.groupby("model")["good"].sum() / best_model = by_model.idxmax() / df.to_csv("report.csv", index=False)
bonus: Try df.describe(), df.sort_values("good", ascending=False).head(3), and df["model"].value_counts().
